title: 3Sum
statement:
Return all distinct triplets [a, b, c] of values from nums (at three different indices) with a + b + c = 0. No duplicate triplets; any order of triplets and of values within each.

Constraints: up to 3,000 elements.
hints: Sort first. Fix the smallest element; what's left is two-sum on a sorted array.
Skip equal neighbours to avoid duplicate triplets.
complexity: O(n²) time, O(1) extra (besides the output and sort)

solution.explanation: Sort. For each i (skipping repeats), find pairs in nums[i+1..] summing to −nums[i] with two pointers that move inward depending on whether the sum is too small or too large; after a hit, skip equal values. O(n²) total, which is optimal up to log factors for this problem.
solution.python:
def three_sum(nums):
    nums = sorted(nums); out = []
    n = len(nums)
    for i in range(n - 2):
        if i and nums[i] == nums[i - 1]:
            continue
        j, k = i + 1, n - 1
        while j < k:
            s = nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k]
            if s < 0: j += 1
            elif s > 0: k -= 1
            else:
                out.append([nums[i], nums[j], nums[k]])
                j += 1
                while j < k and nums[j] == nums[j - 1]: j += 1
                k -= 1
    return out
